summary: A is somewhat preferable, mainly because its seekable-body handling degrades safely and its Upload path preserves more existing Files option behavior. Neither patch satisfies the frozen contract closely enough to merge unchanged.
reasons: A falls back to the existing one-shot behavior when SeekCurrent fails; B instead turns a potentially sendable body, such as a pipe-backed *os.File, into an immediate error.
A carries both WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions into Upload, closer to the contract’s requirement to route through Add and retain its option handling. B drops Files query options entirely.
A’s direct Upload retry test uses an opened file as the source and verifies the multipart filename and content on both attempts, giving stronger coverage of the reported streamed-upload case.

Both violate major requirements: the Upload signature uses a new option interface instead of ...FilesOption, Upload duplicates Add rather than calling it, association APIs are added despite an explicit prohibition, and unrelated retry machinery is changed.
risks_a: Upload has the wrong public signature: ...UploadFileOption rather than ...FilesOption.
Upload calls Raw.Do and duplicates Add’s request and response logic instead of routing through Add.

risks_b: Upload has the wrong public signature, bypasses Add, and omits Files query-option handling.
It adds prohibited association fields, including project_id, plus new validation semantics and multipart helper machinery.

The raw retry change returns an error when a body advertises seeking but cannot report its current offset, regressing previously valid one-shot streams. Its tests also omit an explicit source-reader failure case.
